--- title: "How big should the spoon be?" description: "Five hundred interviews from the whole register named Nigeria's winner 3,967 times in 4,000. Forty thousand from phone owners named it never. El-Rufai had the right objection and quoted the wrong one." date: 2026-08-16 categories: - stats-in-life engine: knitr code-fold: true code-summary: "Show the simulation" # Static listing thumbnail. The post's own figures are plotly and interactive, # so none can serve as one; this is built by _thumbnail.R from the same # simulation, and that script carries the post's guards so the two cannot drift. image: thumbnail.png image-alt: "Four sampling distributions. Two sit on the true value, one broad and one narrow; two more sit together a long way to the right of it, the narrowest of all drawn from forty thousand interviews." --- ## Question Polls put Peter Obi first; he finished third. At 2,000 interviews the margin is ±2.18 points (proof). The miss was 19.29 points (proof). Was the sample too small? ## Claim On TVC, three weeks before the vote, El-Rufai [dismissed the polls](https://guardian.ng/news/el-rufai-debunks-obis-election-win-predictions-calls-opinion-polls-a-joke/): > Opinion polls are distorted... When you have about a 100 million registered voters and you are > sampling 2,000 registered voters or 300 registered voters, your results from day one are > unreliable; they will have high margins of error. He was right that they were wrong. ## Counter-claim His next sentence is the better objection. > Most of these polls, like the one by Bloomberg, ANAP and the one by Okonjo Iweala, all used > telephone. What percentage of registered voters have phone numbers in INEC's records? We have > found out and it's 31 per cent. Only 31 per cent of the register can be telephoned (assume). The simulation prices it. Five hundred, whole register: winner right 3,967 of 4,000 (sim). Forty thousand, phones: winner right 0 of 4,000 (sim). ## Setup NaijaSim is invented: 90,000,000 voters, six zones, four colour-named parties (assume). Phone reach is his 31 per cent (assume). The truth is fixed before anyone is interviewed. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(plotly) comma <- function(x, digits = 0) { formatC(x, format = "f", big.mark = ",", digits = digits) } z <- qnorm(0.975) # 95% two-sided # The post's palette: one hue per stream already exists; these four are the # parties, and ink is the truth line rather than a party. pal <- c("#0f766e", "#0e7490", "#b45309", "#6d28d9") ink <- "#57606a" grid <- "#d7dce1" ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ---- Quoted inputs. Every other number in this post derives from these. ---- # ANAP Foundation / NOIPolls, February 2023; see the method note below. anap_n <- 2000 poll <- c(Obi = 21, Tinubu = 13, Atiku = 10, Kwankwaso = 3, Undecided = 23, Refused = 30) elrufai_n <- 40000 # his own poll, as he described it on air phone_share <- 0.31 # his figure for phone coverage, not checked against INEC # INEC, 2023 presidential election. registered <- 93469008 votes_cast <- 24965218 votes_valid <- 24025940 votes <- c(Obi = 6101533, Tinubu = 8794726, Atiku = 6984520, Kwankwaso = 1496687) # A mistyped input should fail the render rather than publish quietly. stopifnot( sum(poll) == 100, sum(votes) <= votes_valid, votes_valid <= votes_cast, votes_cast <= registered ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Fifty-three of every hundred respondents were undecided or would not say, so the # headline numbers do not sum to anything like a vote share. Comparing with the # result means rebasing onto the respondents who named a candidate. decided <- sum(poll[names(votes)]) poll_obi <- poll[["Obi"]] / decided act_obi <- votes[["Obi"]] / votes_valid miss <- poll_obi - act_obi ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fpc <- sqrt((registered - anap_n) / (registered - 1)) se_anap <- sqrt(poll_obi * (1 - poll_obi) / anap_n) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The sample size at which the margin of error would have been as wide as the # miss, i.e. the only n for which the objection lands. n_cross <- ceiling(z^2 * poll_obi * (1 - poll_obi) / miss^2) ``` ::: ## The simulation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(20260817) sim_party <- c("Green", "Blue", "Red", "Yellow") sim_zone <- c("North West", "North East", "North Central", "South West", "South East", "South South") sim_reg_z <- c(21, 12, 15, 18, 9, 15) * 1e6 # registered voters, by zone names(sim_reg_z) <- sim_zone # The national result, set by fiat. Blue wins. sim_target <- c(Green = 0.30, Blue = 0.38, Red = 0.24, Yellow = 0.08) # Zone shares are chosen, EXCEPT North Central, solved so the register-weighted # truth lands exactly on sim_target. sim_zs <- rbind( c(0.08, 0.50, 0.36, 0.06), c(0.10, 0.52, 0.32, 0.06), c(NA, NA, NA, NA ), c(0.34, 0.34, 0.22, 0.10), c(0.72, 0.12, 0.08, 0.08), c(0.48, 0.26, 0.16, 0.10) ) dimnames(sim_zs) <- list(sim_zone, sim_party) i_nc <- match("North Central", sim_zone) sim_zs[i_nc, ] <- (sum(sim_reg_z) * sim_target - colSums(sim_zs[-i_nc, ] * sim_reg_z[-i_nc])) / sim_reg_z[i_nc] # Phone reach is chosen, EXCEPT South South, solved so national coverage is # exactly the 31 per cent he quoted. The poorest zones reach fewest. sim_reach_z <- c(`North West` = 0.160, `North East` = 0.120, `North Central` = 0.300, `South West` = 0.500, `South East` = 0.440, `South South` = NA)[sim_zone] i_ss <- match("South South", sim_zone) sim_reach_z[i_ss] <- (phone_share * sum(sim_reg_z) - sum((sim_reg_z * sim_reach_z)[-i_ss])) / sim_reg_z[i_ss] # Each zone splits 60/40 into two states leaning opposite ways, so no stratum is # internally uniform. B moves 1.5x as far as A, preserving the zone average; the # 0.5 cap keeps every state inside (0, 1). sim_st <- NULL; sim_reg_s <- numeric(0); sim_szone <- character(0) for (zn in sim_zone) { g <- sim_zs[zn, "Green"]; b <- sim_zs[zn, "Blue"] d <- 0.5 * min(g / 1.5, b) s_a <- sim_zs[zn, ]; s_a["Green"] <- g + d; s_a["Blue"] <- b - d s_b <- sim_zs[zn, ]; s_b["Green"] <- g - 1.5 * d; s_b["Blue"] <- b + 1.5 * d sim_st <- rbind(sim_st, s_a, s_b) sim_reg_s <- c(sim_reg_s, 0.60 * sim_reg_z[[zn]], 0.40 * sim_reg_z[[zn]]) sim_szone <- c(sim_szone, zn, zn) } sim_frame_s <- sim_reg_s * unname(sim_reach_z[sim_szone]) # A mistyped country should fail the render rather than publish quietly. stopifnot( sum(sim_reg_z) == 90e6, all(abs(rowSums(sim_st) - 1) < 1e-12), all(sim_st > 0), all(sim_st < 1), isTRUE(all.equal(colSums(sim_st * sim_reg_s) / sum(sim_reg_s), sim_target)), isTRUE(all.equal(sum(sim_frame_s) / sum(sim_reg_s), phone_share)) ) sim_w_true <- sim_reg_s / sum(sim_reg_s) # a fair poll's weights sim_w_frame <- sim_frame_s / sum(sim_frame_s) # what a phone poll actually gets sim_truth <- colSums(sim_st * sim_w_true) sim_ptruth <- colSums(sim_st * sim_w_frame) sim_frame_N <- sum(sim_frame_s) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Seeded here, not left to the chunk above, so these numbers do not depend on # how many draws the country construction happened to consume. set.seed(20260817) # Largest remainder: proportional shares rounded the obvious way do not sum to n. sim_alloc <- function(n, w) { raw <- n * w; a <- floor(raw); k <- n - sum(a) if (k > 0) { j <- order(raw - a, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(k)]; a[j] <- a[j] + 1 } stopifnot(sum(a) == n) a } SIM_REPS <- 4000 # One rmultinom call per state, vectorised over all 4,000 repetitions. sim_run <- function(n, w) { a <- sim_alloc(n, w) est <- matrix(0, SIM_REPS, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, sim_party)) for (i in seq_along(a)) { if (a[i] == 0) next est <- est + w[i] * t(rmultinom(SIM_REPS, a[i], sim_st[i, ])) / a[i] } est } # "Right" means Blue tops the poll, not merely Blue ahead of Green. sim_summ <- function(est) { g <- 100 * est[, "Green"] c(green = mean(g), sd = sd(g), right = 100 * mean(sim_party[max.col(est, ties.method = "first")] == "Blue")) } sim_ns_fair <- c(n_cross, 100, 250, 500, 1000, anap_n) sim_ns_phone <- c(anap_n, elrufai_n) sim_fair <- lapply(sim_ns_fair, sim_run, w = sim_w_true) sim_phone <- lapply(sim_ns_phone, sim_run, w = sim_w_frame) sim_ft <- t(sapply(sim_fair, sim_summ)) sim_pt <- t(sapply(sim_phone, sim_summ)) # Indexed by value, not position, so the prose survives a reordered ladder. i_win <- match(500, sim_ns_fair) # the rung the argument turns on i_2k <- match(anap_n, sim_ns_fair) j_2k <- match(anap_n, sim_ns_phone) j_40k <- match(elrufai_n, sim_ns_phone) ``` ::: ### What a phone frame actually is Through a phone, Green leads by 3.5 points (sim). In the country, Blue leads by 8 (sim). The figure is not a smaller copy of the country; it is a different country, one that leans Green. ::: {.cell} ::: {#fig-country .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` A phone frame is a different country, leaning Green. ::: ::: *Pattern: each bar is a party, coloured by its name; the phone frame lifts Green and cuts Blue, while the dotted lines mark the country's true shares.* ### The spoon, priced: population size buys nothing Population size is worth 0.0011% of the margin (proof). That is his objection, priced. ::: {.cell} ::: {#fig-spoon-price .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Ninety million voters buy 0.0011% of the margin. ::: ::: *Pattern: the two lines are one line; the shaded sliver is the entire population correction.* ### Four thousand runs: sample size is not the fix Five hundred beats forty thousand, eighty times smaller (sim). The frame never climbs. The ladder: Blue tops 4,000 polls 64% of the time at 500 interviews and 100% at 2,000; never, even at 40,000, on the phone frame. ::: {.cell} ::: {#fig-ladder .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Bigger spoon, same corner. The frame never wins. ::: ::: *Pattern: one line climbs, the other flatlines at zero — the gap is the frame.* ### The same answer, harder: precision without accuracy At 2,000, phones wobble 0.96 points against 0.87 fair (sim). Narrowest, and furthest from the truth. ::: {.cell} ::: {#fig-density .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Narrow, and furthest from the truth. ::: ::: *Pattern: four bell curves, narrowest on the right; the truth lines mark each frame's centre.* ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Where the numbers come from **The margin.** For a proportion $p$ from $n$ draws, $SE=\sqrt{p(1-p)/n}$. Population size enters only through the finite population correction $\sqrt{(N-n)/(N-1)}$, which at $n=2{,}000$ against $N=93{,}469{,}008$ is 0.9999893 — a shrinkage of 0.0011% of the standard error. **The miss.** Obi polled 44.68% of decided respondents and took 25.40% of valid votes: a gap of 19.29 points, or 17.3 standard errors. Inverting the margin for the sample size that would cover a miss that large gives 26 interviews — the rung on the left of the ladder, and the reason the ladder starts there. **The country.** NaijaSim is invented and deliberately not a model of Nigeria. Zone names are real; register, zone splits, parties and result are made up, because verifiable zone-level 2023 figures do not exist from one authoritative source and inventing them while calling them the past would be worse than inventing a country and saying so. Ninety million registered, six zones, four colour-named parties, and coverage of 31% borrowed from his own figure. Seeded at 20260817; 4,000 repetitions at each sample size; stratified by state. **Quoted, not derived.** The El-Rufai quotations are as reported by [The Guardian Nigeria](https://guardian.ng/news/el-rufai-debunks-obis-election-win-predictions-calls-opinion-polls-a-joke/) from *Journalists' Hangout* on TVC News, 4 February 2023. The sample size, phone-based stratified random method and the six percentages come from [ANAP Foundation's press release](https://www.anapfoundation.com/press-releases/2023-elections-peter-obi-maintains-lead-amongst-presidential-poll-respondents); the register and valid votes are INEC's, via the [published breakdown](https://dailypost.ng/2023/03/01/2023-elections-breakdown-of-results-as-tinubu-defeats-atiku-obi/). Outlets differ on the second figure in that first quotation, The Guardian having "300" where [The Cable](https://www.thecable.ng/noi-poll-weve-been-using-same-methodology-since-2015-anap-foundation-replies-critics/) reports "three thousand"; the arithmetic uses ANAP's published 2,000, so nothing turns on it. His own 40,000-sample poll has no published methodology I could find, and appears here as a sample size and nothing else. **The portrait.** `File:Nasir Ahmed el-Rufai 2023.jpg` on Wikimedia Commons, 470 × 662, tagged PD-VOA: a Voice of America work, so public domain in the United States rather than openly licensed. The Commons page records it as a VOA Africa upload, which is what makes the tag stick. **Attribution, split deliberately.** That accuracy depends on absolute sample size rather than on the sampling fraction is standard, and Freedman, Pisani and Purves develop it in the chapter on chance errors in sampling in *Statistics*. The soup-and-spoon comparison is attributed to [George Gallup](https://nrich.maths.org/13895), not to them, because I could not verify that the book uses the soup wording. ::: ::: {.aside-box .hommie} > So five hundred people told you who won, and forty thousand did not? Yes. The five hundred got it right and the forty thousand got it wrong, every run. A spoon that never reaches the bottom scoops the top faster. :::
